text:
maria: Hey infra, seeing elevated local NVMe latency on gpu-pool-us-east nodes after last week's batch rollout. 95th token latency spikes ~300ms and some batch jobs are timing out.
alex: Which nodes exactly? IOPS or latency metrics? any SMART errors showing up?
maria: gpu-us-east-34, gpu-us-east-35, gpu-us-east-36. iostat shows device util ~99%, avgqu-sz ~80 on /dev/nvme0n1. SMART output has rising media_errors and Wear_Leveling_Count drift on a couple drives. snippet:
```bash
smartctl -A /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep 'Media|Wear|Temp'
  Media_Error_Count     10
  Percentage_Used       14
  Temperature_Celsius   48
```
devin: saw something similar yesterday after the nightly cleanup. overlay snapshot deletions (rm -rf /mnt/ephemeral/snap-*) ran in parallel across many pods. Massive metadata/fsync storms. Cleaner is doing too many concurrent deletes.
infra-bot: Note: ephemeral-cleaner backoff patch is currently scheduled for canary rollout next window. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ephemeral-cleaner
taylor-oncall: Let's avoid mass deletes during compactions. Proposal: add randomized jitter and cap parallel deletes per host to 4. Also run deletes under ionice/nice to reduce scheduling impact. To reproduce locally use:
```bash
fio --name=meta -rw=randrw -bs=4k -iodepth=32 -numjobs=4
```
alex: Also, ops spotted thermal warnings in host logs — drives in racks 7-9 report high temperature spikes -> possible thermal throttling which increases write amplification and accelerates wear. I've opened a DC ticket to reseat fans and check airflow.
maria: For short-term mitigation I'll patch the cleaner to `--delete-concurrency=4` and add per-shard jitter (30-120s). Deploy to canary now.
devin: On test nodes, tuning blk-mq (reducing nr_requests) and lowering queue depth reduced avgqsz and 95th latency. We should try conservative queue tuning for these devices.
taylor-oncall: If SMART crosses failing thresholds, mark drives for replacement. Suggest replacement criteria: Percentage_Used increase >12% over baseline or media_errors >3. Budget estimate: ~$800 per NVMe → ~12 nodes = ~$9.6k immediate spend if needed.
infra-bot: Patch deployed to canary (gpu-us-east-34) at 18:11 UTC. Monitoring alerts for iostat and smartctl enabled and hooked to #monitoring.
maria: Thanks — will post before/after graphs in #monitoring in ~2h. If 95th spikes persist we'll schedule drains and maintenance windows for affected nodes. :thumbsup:
